rules.clause: Article 15(1) & (4): Robustness, Cybersecurity and Resistance to Adversarial Exploitation
rules.title: Direct Prompt Injection & System Override Defense
rules.description: High-risk AI systems must be resilient against third-party attempts to alter their output, bypass guardrails, or exploit vulnerabilities through prompt injection.

rules.clause: Article 15(1): Resilience against System Prompt Extraction
rules.title: System Prompt & Intellectual Property Exfiltration
rules.description: AI models must prevent unauthorized disclosure of underlying system prompts, proprietary guardrails, and operational context to untrusted users.

rules.clause: Control A.8.4: Robustness and Resilience of AI Systems
rules.title: Indirect Prompt Injection in Retrieved Context (RAG)
rules.description: Systems utilizing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) must sanitize or neutralize untrusted data retrieved from external documents to prevent secondary injection payloads.

rules.clause: Measure 2.7: AI System Security and Resilience against Attacks
rules.title: Jailbreak & Safety Boundary Bypass
rules.description: AI systems shall be evaluated against roleplay-based and hypothetical jailbreak attacks that coerce the model into generating harmful, dangerous, or illegal content.

rules.clause: GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) & DPDP Sec. 8: Data Minimization & PII Leakage
rules.title: Unmasked Personal Identifiable Information (PII) in Local Datasets
rules.description: Datasets, prompts, and log stores must not contain plaintext personal identifiers (credit cards, SSNs, personal emails, phone numbers) without explicit tokenization or masking.

rules.clause: Control A.9.2: Access Control and Operational Boundaries
rules.title: Unrestricted Arbitrary Code Execution / Tool Abuse
rules.description: AI agent tool definitions must not expose arbitrary shell commands, raw code eval, or un-sandboxed system access to autonomous model invocation.

rules.clause: Manage 2.4: Privacy Risk Mitigation & PII Regeneration
rules.title: Model PII Regeneration via Targeted Probes
rules.description: Models must not memorize or regurgitate training data containing personal confidential records when queried with targeted prefixes.

rules.clause: GDPR Art. 32: Security of Processing — Credential Exposure
rules.title: Exposed API Keys and Secrets in Source or Environment Configs
rules.description: API keys, bearer tokens, and private connection credentials must never reside in source control, prompt templates, or unencrypted local files.
